query: For additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 high-entropy alloy with an fcc matrix, what testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs degradation during elevated-temperature exposure to oxidizing or reducing gases and why catastrophic failure may occur? Specify a controlled change that would reveal the governing behavior, predicted observations relative to the starting-state baseline, applicable exposure boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: Catastrophic failure during elevated-temperature exposure in AM Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 originates from rapid formation of an interconnected intergranular oxide network driven by selective oxidation of Ti and Al at grain boundaries. This network embrittles the matrix, concentrates stresses, and nucleates cracks that coalesce under thermal cycling.
generation.material_initial_state: As-built additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 HEA with single-phase fcc matrix, no pre‐existing oxide scale, equiaxed grains (~50 µm)
generation.intervention: Reduce Ti content from 0.3 at.% to 0.2 at.% while keeping other elements constant in otherwise identical AM processing
generation.conditions: Exposure to oxidizing gas (air) at 700 °C for 100 h under ambient pressure (PO2≈0.21 atm), followed by 50 thermal cycles between 700 °C and 25 °C
generation.structural_mediator: Intergranular oxide network thickness and continuity at prior‐particle boundaries
generation.mechanism: Lower Ti slows the nucleation and growth of Ti‐rich oxides at grain boundaries, preventing a continuous brittle oxide network and thus reducing embrittlement and crack initiation
generation.predicted_outcome: Ti‐reduced alloy will exhibit ≥30% thinner intergranular oxide films and ≥50% fewer grain‐boundary cracks after exposure and cycling compared to baseline
generation.baseline: Original Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy after identical exposure: continuous intergranular oxide network ~2 µm thick, average crack density ~10 cracks/mm
generation.boundary: Valid for exposures between 600 °C and 800 °C in oxidizing atmospheres (PO2=0.1–0.21 atm) for 10–1000 h; does not address purely reducing environments
generation.uncertainty: High—no direct prior data on Ti‐content effects in this specific HEA; quantitative effect sizes are estimates

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two AM builds of Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 and Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.2; expose both to air at 700 °C for 100 h with 50 thermal cycles. Characterize intergranular oxide thickness and crack density via cross‐sectional SEM and image analysis.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If Ti‐reduced alloy does not show ≥20% reduction in both intergranular oxide thickness and crack density relative to baseline, the hypothesis is falsified.
